messages:
mia: Heads-up — noticed a sharp p99 TTFT bump on the token-level SLI panel for us-west1 around 14:03 UTC. p50/p95 look fine but p99 moved from ~120ms to ~420ms for a ~10min window.

mia: Panel: Grafana > Token-SLI > ttft_by_model_shard (row 3). Screenshot attached in thread.

arjun: did tokens/sec dip at the same time? sometimes a throughput drop + queueing = tail latency.

mia: tokens/sec actually dropped ~30% for a subset of model_shard tags. Here's the quick prom query I used:
```
sum by (region, model_shard) (rate(tokens_consumed_total{region="us-west1"}[1m]))
```

leo: metric-bot fired NAT gateway egress errors around the same time (lots of TCP retransmits on fleet subnets). Could be networking packet loss causing slow kv cache reads.

metric-bot: ALERT nat-egress-errors-usw1 firing (count > 50 in 5m). See /alerts/2319.

sara: hmm also see an extreme rise in tag cardinality on the dashboard: the panel was accidentally grouped by `route_id` which exploded when synthetic load hit. High-cardinality groups can make percentile panels noisy.

mia: good catch — the dashboard had `by (region, model_shard, route_id)`. I removed route_id in an ad-hoc duplicate panel and the p99 noise mostly vanished.

arjun: so two things: (1) real network blips (NAT) causing some requests to tail; (2) dashboard grouping made a small noisy slice dominant and looked like global regression. We should avoid route_id in alerting aggregation.

leo: proposal for dashboard changes:
- change queries to `by (region, model_family)` instead of model_shard when used for global SLOs
- add a small per-shard heatmap row to debug hotspotting
- explicit panel query to drop high-cardinality labels: `label_replace` or `without(route_id)`

sara: for the alert rule: currently it fires on `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by(le, region, model_shard) (rate(ttft_bucket[5m]))) > 0.3` (seconds). We should:
1) require sustained 5m window + tokens/sec below baseline: add `and on(region, model_family) (sum by(region, model_family)(rate(tokens_consumed_total[5m])) < 5000)`
2) exclude route_id from grouping

mia: example adjusted PromQL (draft):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum without(route_id) (rate(ttft_bucket{region="us-west1"}[5m]))) > 0.35
and on(region, model_family) (
  sum by(region, model_family) (rate(tokens_consumed_total[5m])) < 4500
)
```

arjun: nice. Also add `for: 10m` on the alert to avoid alert storms from 1-off flaps.

leo: ops runbook tweak: when p99 alert triggers, check (1) nat-egress-errors and tcp_retransmits, (2) tokens/sec heatmap, (3) kvcache-evictions per shard. Quick triage checklist in the alert `runbook_url`.

mia: I'll patch the dashboard to: remove route_id grouping for SLO panels, add a per-shard heatmap and a small tokens/sec sparkline in the header. Will open a tiny PR and ping y'all.

sara: also add a Grafana annotation for the NAT incident time window so future drifts are easier to correlate.

mia: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/dashboards/pull/842 — changes: ttft panels (use without(route_id)), new heatmap, alert rule tweak (draft). PTAL.

metric-bot: Deploy job started: infra-dashboard-sync v2.1 -> staging (sha: a3f9).

arjun: LGTM — after landing, let's observe for 24h then decide if we need longer alert `for` or token/sec thresholds.

mia: +1. Thanks all. Closing the loop once PR merged and alerts stabilize. :thumbsup:
